title: ARC Scaling Challenge: An Open Falsification Toolkit for Recursive-Amplification Scaling Laws
description: An open toolkit and protocol set for testing, and attempting to falsify, claims about sequential versus parallel recursion scaling (the ARC Principle). It provides alpha and beta estimators, AIC and BIC model selection, reproducible protocols and synthetic example data. In the programme's own runs (Paper II), the error-decay exponent, which describes how error falls as recursive depth grows, stayed near zero for parallel recursion in DeepSeek R1 and GPT-5.4, and sequential exceeded parallel (descriptive; no interval). The one smoothly scaling model's sequential fit, about 0.49 by regression, is inconclusive. These are not measurements of the capability exponent of Law I, the ARC Principle, and super-linear scaling has not been observed. The early single-model estimate of about 2.24 (DeepSeek R1) is retracted. Sharma and Chopra (2025) report that sequential scaling outperforms parallel self-consistency at matched compute, and no priority is claimed for that result. Their paper is arXiv:2511.02309. The bare d/(d+1) exponent is acknowledged prior art, and the protocols are designs written before the theory registration of 8 September 2026, none of them a registered test. Researchers are invited to replicate or refute.
notes: Companion repository: arc-principle-validation (papers, results, harness). Canonical research hub: https://www.michaeldariuseastwood.com/research/
